chapter: Trumpet teachers and St. Louis heroes
title: Creath and Marable feature rival soloists
summary: Creath featured trumpeter Bob Shoffner and Marable featured pianist Burroughs Lovingood. Thomas and Dance compare this to King Oliver featuring Louis Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: You know performers and people are the greatest people in the world. Not because I'm one of them because I think young. I've seen some tremendous things happen. They brought a fellow in -- I think he worked for Joe Oliver in Chicago -- by the name of Bob Shoffner (?) and featured him. Do you dig up one trumpet player if he's a trumpet player. Can you feature one piano if he's another piano player.
Oh, who did Bob work for then?
Charlie Creath. Dig what I'm talking about?
And I take it that Creath could cut in.
I don't know. He didn't seem to mind.
Yeah. And, Fate brought in a fellow by the name of Burroughs Lovinggood.
Yeah, yeah. And, he featured him. Isn't that something.
The thing is, of course, that's what Joe Oliver did with Louis, too, isn't it?
Well, yeah. I think that's the respect of one artist to another.
